subject: Request: exec payback authorization for BrightHealth prefetch regression
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: exec payback authorization for BrightHealth prefetch regression

Hi Karthik / Laura —

Quick context: BrightHealth (HSP-4821) went live with our prefetch + KV cache in early September. They ramped traffic aggressively and this month we surfaced a regression in prefetch K/V handling that caused elevated latencies and a partial throttle fallback for ~72 hours (see attached support_timeline_20261011.pdf). Customer impact: increased per-token cost and several 5xx errors during peak windows; they paused a planned feature launch tied to our routing optimization.

Customer request: BrightHealth has asked for a commercial remediation while we finish the KV-prefetch patch. They are asking for a one-time credit to offset the incremental cost and program delay. Sales recommends a one-time payback equal to the estimated incremental spend ($75,000) plus a goodwill credit to preserve the renewal cadence.

Ask: I need exec-level authorization to offer a one-time payback/credit for BrightHealth. Proposed options:
- Option A (recommended): One-time credit of $75k applied to next invoice + 30 days of waived overage charges;
- Option B (conservative): 60% of A ($45k) applied as a compute credit, with a 60-day service credit cap;
- Option C: No credit; offer extended support SLAs + priority fix schedule (risk of churn).

Why exec approval is required: the deal is an enterprise reserved capacity contract with a multi-quarter renewal planned; this is outside delegated sales discount authority. Finance and sales ops need signoff to proceed with a commercial remediation and a DocuSign amendment.

I attached a proposed payback calc (proposed_payback_calc.xlsx) and the support timeline. I can draft the exact amendment after we land on amount and approach.

Next steps suggested: Karthik/Laura — please confirm whether Product considers the regression severity sufficient to warrant the ask, and whether the targeted patch (prefetch KV fix) is on the verified schedule for mid-November. Aditya — FYI on the numbers; please chime on accounting treatment and approval chain.

Neha
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: exec payback authorization for BrightHealth prefetch regression

Neha — thanks for the summary and attachments. A few clarifying points from Product: 

1) Root cause & timeline: We traced the regression to a race in the KV prefetch pipeline when large prefix loads coincide with autoscale events. The engineering owner has prioritized a fix; current ETA for the patch + regression test is 2026-11-15. If we keep to that date, the customer impact window is ~4 weeks more.

2) Scope of impact: Do we have the breakdown of incremental token costs vs. credit owed? The XLS looks like an estimate; I want to ensure we’re not double-counting the cost reductions that will come with the patch.

3) Product stance: I think a one-time commercial accommodation is reasonable to preserve the relationship, but I want to avoid setting a precedent where credits are automatic for all prefetch regressions. Can we make this approval conditional on three items: (a) documented postmortem, (b) firm patch ETA and rollback plan, and (c) public facing note on what we fixed (so customer perceives value)?

If Sales is comfortable with those conditions, Product supports Option A conditional on the postmortem + ETA.

Karthik
VP, Product — Serving Runtime
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: exec payback authorization for BrightHealth prefetch regression

Adding finance perspective — thanks for the thorough write-up. A few notes: 

- Accounting / recognition: A one-time credit can be handled as a contra-revenue credit. We prefer credits tied to a documented remediation and a single amendment that references the postmortem.
- Amount guidance: Given contract size and churn risk, finance would greenlight up to 60% of the proposed $75k ($45k) under delegated authority. Anything above that requires an exec sign-off (COO/CRO).
- Controls: Please include a clause in the amendment that the credit is a one-time remediation for the documented incident and does not change committed capacity or future pricing.

Suggested next step: Neha — if we proceed with Option A (preferred by Product and CS), can you escalate to Laura and include a short one-paragraph rationale for the exec packet? I can prep the amortization/accounting note for review.

Aditya
Head of Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 16:27:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Request: exec payback authorization for BrightHealth prefetch regression

Laura — forwarding the thread with Product + Finance input. TL;DR: Product supports Option A conditional on postmortem + ETA (11/15). Finance will approve up to $45k under delegation; anything above needs your OK. Customer outcome risk is moderate — they paused a major feature launch tied to our route optimizer. 

Suggested exec packet blurb (one paragraph for approval request):

"BrightHealth (HSP-4821) experienced a prefetch KV regression that caused elevated latencies and increased token spend over a ~72-hour window in early October, delaying a customer feature launch. Product has scheduled a fix with ETA 2026-11-15 and will provide a formal postmortem. To preserve the renewal trajectory and offset measurable incremental spend, Customer Success recommends a one-time commercial remediation. Finance supports a $45k credit under delegated authority; approval is requested to offer the recommended $75k one-time credit (or downward-modified amount) as a one-time contract amendment, contingent on postmortem and fixed ETA."

Please advise whether you will (A) approve the full $75k as proposed, (B) approve finance's delegated $45k, or (C) decline and we proceed with enhanced SLAs / priority remediation wording. If you approve A/B, I will prepare the DocuSign amendment (link to be provided) and communications plan.

Neha
(attachments referenced: support_timeline_20261011.pdf, proposed_payback_calc.xlsx)
